It is completely understandable to feel torn about holiday visits, especially when your relationship with your parents lacks emotional support. Navigating family expectations can be incredibly stressful, and it is okay to prioritize your own mental well-being. You are not obligated to put yourself in a situation that causes you distress, but it is also natural to worry about the potential fallout of setting that boundary.

When making your decision, try to weigh the emotional cost of attending against the stress of their reaction if you stay home. If you decide not to go, you can keep your explanation brief and firm, such as saying you are taking time to rest this season. If you feel you must attend to avoid a larger conflict, consider setting strict boundaries to protect yourself—like staying at a hotel, limiting the length of your visit, or having a clear exit strategy. Whatever you choose, remember that protecting your peace is a valid and important decision.
